counting_rule: DSM-5-TR Criterion A requires TWO OR MORE of five numbered items, and at least one must be item 1, 2 or 3. That is a counting threshold with an additional gate, so each numbered item is a separately scored unit. Criterion B is a separate requirement of the diagnosis and carries no counting threshold: it lists major life areas as examples and asks for at least one, so it is ILLUSTRATIVE and is satisfied by marked dysfunction in any ONE named area. A diagnosis requires Criterion A AND Criterion B.
scored_grain_note: Six judged units: the five counted items A1 to A5, plus Criterion B at criterion grain. B was added on 2026-07-28 and is PROVISIONAL: judged in the run, reported separately, and included in breadth only under the opt-in arm. The criteria this project aborts are ONSET, DURATION and EXCLUSION, because mouse annotation cannot express morbidity timing, episode length or a differential diagnosis. Criteria C to F are exactly those and remain unscored.

items.floor_reason: A delusion is a belief with propositional content. No organism-level mouse analog exists under any vocabulary. construct_inadmissible.
items.dsm_definition: A delusion is a firmly held belief that does not shift when the person meets evidence against it. Themes vary, for example being persecuted, things referring to oneself, the body, religion or grandiosity. The most frequent kind is persecutory, the belief that some person, organization or group will hurt or harass one. Also frequent is the referential kind, the belief that gestures, remarks or things in the surroundings are aimed at oneself.
items.dsm_definition_source: DSM-5-TR, Key Features That Define the Psychotic Disorders

items.floor_reason: A hallucination is a percept without a stimulus, reportable only by the experiencer. No mouse analog. construct_inadmissible.
items.dsm_definition: Hallucinations are experiences like perceptions that arise with no outside stimulus. They feel vivid and clear, as forceful as ordinary perception, and the person cannot control them at will. Any sense can be involved, but in schizophrenia and related disorders hearing is the commonest, usually as voices, known or unknown, that the person experiences as separate from their own thoughts.
items.dsm_definition_source: DSM-5-TR, Key Features That Define the Psychotic Disorders

items.floor_reason: Mice have no speech. Ultrasonic vocalization syntax is a remote non-criterion proxy and is NOT admitted as strict. construct_inadmissible.
items.dsm_definition: Formal thought disorder, that is, disorganized thinking, is usually judged from how the person speaks. The person may jump between topics (derailment, loose associations), may answer questions only indirectly or not to the point at all (tangentiality), and in rare severe cases may speak so disjointedly that the speech can hardly be understood, much like the language of receptive aphasia (incoherence, sometimes called word salad).
items.dsm_definition_source: DSM-5-TR, Key Features That Define the Psychotic Disorders

items.note: Partially modellable and explicitly BIDIRECTIONAL: the item names grossly disorganized OR catatonic behavior, so both catalepsy, waxy flexibility, immobility and stupor at one pole, and hyperlocomotion and stereotypy at the other, are organism-level analogs.
items.dsm_definition: Motor behavior that is grossly disorganized or abnormal can take many forms, from childlike silliness to agitation that cannot be predicted. Any kind of goal-directed behavior can be affected, so that everyday activities become hard to carry out. Catatonic behavior is a marked fall in how much the person responds to the surroundings. It runs from resisting instructions (negativism), through holding a rigid, inappropriate or odd posture, to giving no verbal or motor response at all (mutism and stupor).
items.dsm_definition_source: DSM-5-TR, Key Features That Define the Psychotic Disorders

items.note: Most modellable. The item's own parenthetical names diminished emotional expression and avolition. Absorbs asociality and social withdrawal.
items.dsm_definition: Two negative symptoms stand out in schizophrenia: reduced emotional expression and avolition. Reduced emotional expression means less emotion shown in the face, less eye contact, flatter speech melody (prosody), and fewer of the gestures of the hands, head and face that normally add emotional emphasis to what is said. Avolition is a drop in purposeful activity that the person starts and sustains from their own motivation.
items.dsm_definition_source: DSM-5-TR, Key Features That Define the Psychotic Disorders

items.components_provenance: Paraphrased by the project in DSM5_paraphrased/SCZ_criteria.txt. The names below are the construct names that text uses, listed for the component field only.
items.note: WHAT THIS CRITERION ASKS FOR IS DETERIORATION, NOT A TRAIT DIFFERENCE. DSM asks whether functioning in a major life area is markedly below the level the individual previously achieved, or, for onset in childhood or adolescence, whether an expected level was never achieved. Both readings are about a CHANGE or a FAILURE TO ARRIVE, not about a stable characteristic. A mouse phenotype that is a constant lifelong difference from wild type is the weakest form of this criterion; one that emerges or worsens after development is the strongest. RECORD WHICH ONE YOU ARE LOOKING AT, because the project measures the size of this substitution rather than assuming it. Set qualifier_absent=false when the term itself names emergence, progression, deterioration, age-dependence or a loss of a previously present capacity. Set qualifier_absent=true when the term names only a stable between-genotype difference and is therefore standing in for a deterioration that MGI does not state. Do not default to either. THE BOUNDARY WITH A5, WHICH YOU MUST NOT COLLAPSE. A5 names the SYMPTOM, diminished emotional expression and avolition. B names the CONSEQUENCE at the level of major life areas: work, interpersonal relations, self-care, academic and occupational functioning. Many mouse terms can be read either way. Assign your best single unit in item_id, and when a term genuinely instantiates both, record the other in second_item_id rather than silently choosing one.

excluded_criteria.B: Level of functioning below premorbid. Not scored per D3: a mouse has no premorbid baseline.
excluded_criteria.C: Six month duration. Not a symptom.
excluded_criteria.D: Schizoaffective and mood exclusion. Not a symptom.
excluded_criteria.E: Substance and medical exclusion. Not a symptom.
excluded_criteria.F: ASD and communication disorder qualifier. Not a symptom.

mechanism_note: The aberrant-salience endophenotype (prepulse inhibition, sensorimotor gating, latent inhibition, psychotomimetic hyper-response to amphetamine, MK-801 or PCP) must NEVER be strict-admissible for any Criterion A item. It is the mechanism axis. The term-attribution probe showed prepulse inhibition plus sensorimotor gating alone carry 57 percent of Phenodigm's best matches on SCZ, and endophenotype plus circuit carriers about 80 percent, so this separation is exactly what makes the FACET minus Phenodigm gap interpretable rather than a loss.
satisfaction_rule: COUNTED. A scored item is met only by a match to THAT item. Diagnostic gate: at least two of A1 to A5, and at least one of those must be A1, A2 or A3. Breadth denominator is 5 individually-matched units.
comparability_note: Breadth denominators differ across disorders (ASD 7, SCZ 5, ID 2, NCD 2) AND the units differ in difficulty, because DSM counts enumerated items in ASD and SCZ but accepts a single example in ID and NCD. Report fraction of scored units met alongside the raw count, and never rank disorders on raw breadth.
provisional_note: Criterion B is JUDGED IN THE RUN exactly like every other unit, and whether it counts toward breadth is a downstream aggregation switch, not a prompt difference. The classifier is not told B is provisional, so the opt-in and opt-out comparison differs only in the roll-up. Primary reporting uses the denominator of 5; the opt-in arm uses 6 and is reported beside it, never instead of it. The reason B is provisional rather than primary: schizophrenia is defined clinically by its symptoms, and functional deterioration establishes clinical significance rather than being an additional symptom class. Mouse analogues of deterioration can strengthen a model, but they are not direct models of Criterion B and must not be labelled as such. Use score_breadth.py to compute both.
variant_note: PRODUCTION VARIANT. Identical to SCZ.json except that scored units carry a paraphrase of DSM-5-TR's own definitions. Source: DSM-5-TR, Key Features That Define the Psychotic Disorders (definitional).
